title: latency-aware queue fairness stabilizer and timeout backoff for continuous batcher
author: Nina Patel
description: Motivation: Continuous batching reduces per-token cost but is sensitive to long-tail requests and probe-induced starvation. In canary environments we observed intermittent 95th/99th percentile latency spikes during heavy KV-miss patterns and probe timeouts. This PR introduces a latency-aware admission stabilizer that reduces oscillation and explicit exponential timeout backoff for probe/reservation attempts to prevent repeated probe storms. Design summary: 1) Stabilizer: a lightweight controller in the continuous batcher admission path that tracks a short sliding-window of per-queue observed service latency and dynamically adjusts admission probability and slot reservation time. The goal is to smooth short-term bursts while preserving fairness across workload cohorts. 2) Timeout backoff: probes (lease/slot probes, KV warmup probes) transition to an exponential backoff on repeated failures rather than retrying at a fixed interval. This prevents thundering retries when a downstream resource (KV or GPU kernel queue) is congested. 3) KV-cache pin heuristic: when the stabilizer detects repeated wait/evict cycles for KV-pinned entries, the cache adaptor applies a short-term pin-decay extension to reduce eviction churn for hot keys. Implementation notes: - New runtime/scheduler/latency_stabilizer.go implements the stabilizer controller; it exposes two tunables: observation_window_ms and admission_smoothing (alpha). The controller runs lock-free read paths for the hot path and uses a sampled eviction metric to limit overhead. - Batcher changes in runtime/batcher/continuous_batcher.go wire the stabilizer into admission decisions and add a per-request admission token that carries the observed_cohort tag for cohort-aware smoothing. - Probe timeouts moved to runtime/batcher/timeout_backoff.go; exponential backoff starts at base_ms and caps at max_ms; a jitter factor is applied to avoid synchronization. - KV cache changes in runtime/kv/pin_heuristic.go: a short-lived pin extension (heuristic) is applied when eviction churn crosses a threshold. - Tests: added deterministic scheduler unit tests and small integration test that simulates KV miss storms under controlled latency. Benchmarks: microbench harness (bench/latency_stabilizer_bench.go) shows median latency unchanged, P95 improved by ~9% and P99 improved by ~18% under a heavy KV-miss tail synthetic workload. Rollout plan: feature gates behind runtime flag continuous_batcher.stabilizer.enabled=false by default; canary enabled for staging then ramp to 25% traffic in production. Observability: new metrics continuous_batcher.stabilizer.{window_latency_ms,admit_rate} and probe.backoff.{attempts,active_backoffs} plus alerts for sustained backoff > 30s. Backward compatibility: no public API changes; knobs are runtime-only. Risks and mitigations: - Aggressive smoothing could increase median latency for latency-sensitive single-request flows: mitigated by cohort-aware admission and opt-out via route-level annotation. - Backoff could delay recovery for transient faults: capped max backoff and jitter reduces worst-case. See linked LINEAR items for rollout tracking and follow-up work. This description is intentionally compact; details and code comments contain the tuning rationale and references to the microbench harness used in validation.

release_notes: Added latency-aware admission stabilizer to continuous batcher to reduce P95/P99 spikes under heavy KV-miss workloads.
Implemented exponential timeout backoff for probe/retry logic to avoid probe storms.
Improved KV cache pin heuristic to reduce eviction churn for hot keys.
Feature is off by default and gated behind continuous_batcher.stabilizer.enabled; canary rollout recommended.
